_meta.author: Kaylan von Papen
_meta.scope: Pricing and terms only. These verdicts judge how a vendor sells, not how the software performs. We have not run usability testing and do not pretend to.
_meta.rule: Every claim traces to data/pricing_seed.json or data/hidden_costs.json, both read off vendor pricing pages. No invented usage experience, no 'we tested' language.
_meta.why_hand_written: Template-generated verdicts are the exact thin-content pattern that got 1,053 pages noindexed. build_transparency_ratings.py refuses to run if any scored tool lacks a hand-written verdict, so this file cannot quietly fall behind the data.

asana.headline: The pricing page does everything right
asana.body: Free for up to ten people, then $13.49 a seat. No minimum, no setup fee, no card to start, and the annual discount is a modest 23% rather than a penalty for staying flexible. There is nothing hidden here, which is rarer than it should be.
asana.best_for: Teams who want to grow into a paid plan on their own schedule.
asana.watch_for: The jump from Starter to Advanced is more than double, at $30.49 a seat.

datadog.headline: Enterprise monitoring with a genuinely honest price page
datadog.body: A free tier, $15 a seat for Pro, $23 for Enterprise, and the annual price is exactly twelve times the monthly. No commitment premium at all. For a category that usually hides behind 'contact sales', publishing every number is a real choice.
datadog.best_for: Anyone who wants to know the bill before talking to a salesperson.
datadog.watch_for: Host and volume-based charges sit outside per-seat pricing. The seat price is not the whole bill.

linear.headline: The cleanest pricing in the set
linear.body: Free up to 250 issues and ten users, $8 a seat for Basic, $14 for Business. Annual costs exactly twelve monthlies, so there is no penalty for month-to-month. Three plans, three numbers, no asterisks.
linear.best_for: Small engineering teams that want to start free and pay monthly.
linear.watch_for: The free tier's 250-issue ceiling arrives faster than you expect.

stripe.headline: No subscription at all, which sidesteps every trap here
stripe.body: There is no monthly fee. You pay 2.9% plus 30 cents per successful card charge. That scores full marks on our rubric almost by definition, because there is no seat, no tier and no commitment to hide anything inside.
stripe.best_for: Anyone who would rather pay per transaction than per month.
stripe.watch_for: Percentage pricing is not free pricing. At volume the effective cost can exceed a flat fee, and our rubric does not measure that.

1password.headline: Honest pricing, but no free tier to fall back on
1password.body: $2.99 for an individual, $7.99 a seat for Business, annual priced at exactly twelve months. No minimum, no card for the trial, no surcharges. The one point it drops is the absence of a permanently free plan, so eventually you pay.
1password.best_for: Teams who want a straight per-seat price with no commitment games.
1password.watch_for: The Teams Starter Pack is a flat $19.95 for up to ten people, which undercuts per-seat Business for small teams. It is easy to miss.

clickup.headline: Free forever is real, but monthly billing costs you
clickup.body: The free plan is genuinely usable and Unlimited is $10 a seat. The catch is the annual gap: Business is $19 monthly but works out at $12 a seat on the annual plan, so paying month to month costs 58% more. That is a commitment premium, not a discount.
clickup.best_for: Teams confident enough to commit to a year up front.
clickup.watch_for: Budget on the monthly rate if you might leave. The advertised price is usually the annual one.

notion.headline: Transparent until you reach Enterprise
notion.body: Free tier, $12 a seat for Plus, $18 for Business, and only a 20% annual gap. All good. Then Enterprise is quote-only, which is the single point it drops. One hidden tier in an otherwise fully published range.
notion.best_for: Teams who will live in the published tiers and never need a quote.
notion.watch_for: If Enterprise is where you are heading, budget blind. There is no public number.

monday-com.headline: The advertised price is never the price you pay
monday-com.body: Basic reads as $14 a seat. You cannot buy fewer than three, so the real floor is $42 a month. Monday.com states the minimum plainly on the page, which is more than some do, but the headline number is still for a purchase you are not allowed to make.
monday-com.best_for: Teams of three or more, where the minimum costs you nothing.
monday-com.watch_for: Solo users and pairs. You will pay for a seat you do not use.

salesforce.headline: Prices published, but only one plan can be paid monthly
salesforce.body: Starter Suite at $25 is billed monthly or annually. Everything above it, from Pro Suite at $100 through to Max at $550, is billed annually only. That $100 a seat is really $1,200 a seat, due up front. The number on the page is a monthly rate for an annual product.
salesforce.best_for: Buyers with the cash and the certainty to commit for a year.
salesforce.watch_for: The tier names changed in 2026. Enterprise and Unlimited are gone, replaced by Core, Advanced and Max at higher prices.

shopify.headline: Clear tiers, steep climb, meaningful annual gap
shopify.body: $39 for Basic, $105 for Shopify, $399 for Advanced, all published with no minimum and no setup fee. Monthly billing costs 34% more than annual, which is on the punishing side of a discount without being outrageous.
shopify.best_for: Merchants who know which tier they need and will stay a year.
shopify.watch_for: Transaction fees sit on top of the subscription and vary by payment method. The plan price is not the total.

pipedrive.headline: Straightforward CRM pricing with one sharp catch
pipedrive.body: Five published tiers from $24 to $129, no minimum, no setup fee, trial without a card. The problem is the annual gap: Essential is $24 monthly but $14 a seat annually, so staying flexible costs 71% more. That is the widest gap here after HubSpot.
pipedrive.best_for: Teams committing annually, where the effective price is genuinely competitive.
pipedrive.watch_for: No free tier. Once the trial ends you are paying.

semrush.headline: Priced honestly, but the trial wants your card
semrush.body: Pro at $139.95, Guru at $249.95, Business at $499.95, all published, no minimum, and annual pricing that does not punish monthly buyers. The point it loses is the card requirement on the seven-day trial, which turns a trial into a subscription you have to remember to cancel.
semrush.best_for: Buyers who were going to pay anyway and want the numbers up front.
semrush.watch_for: Diarise the trial end date. Card-up-front trials bill by default.

tresorit.headline: Solid personal pricing, a three-seat floor for business
tresorit.body: Personal plans at $11.99 and $19.99 are clean. Business Standard reads as $14.50 a seat but requires three, so the real entry point is $43.50 a month. No free tier either, so there is no way to sit still without paying.
tresorit.best_for: Individuals, or business teams already at three or more people.
tresorit.watch_for: The seat minimum, and a 25% premium for paying monthly.

hubspot.headline: The published price is less than half the first-year cost
hubspot.body: Sales Hub Professional advertises $100 a seat. Onboarding is a required $1,500 on top, so year one for one seat is $2,700 rather than $1,200. Enterprise onboarding is $3,500. Starter has the widest monthly penalty we found anywhere: $7 a seat annually against $20 monthly, so paying monthly costs 186% more.
hubspot.best_for: Buyers on the genuinely free tools, or committing annually with the onboarding fee already budgeted.
hubspot.watch_for: The onboarding fee. It is disclosed, but it is one line under a very large price.

ahrefs.headline: Lowest score here, and not because it is expensive
ahrefs.body: No free tier and no trial, so there is no way to evaluate it without paying. Each plan includes exactly one user and extra seats cost $40 to $80 a month on top. Enterprise requires an annual commitment at $14,990. Every one of those is a published, honest fact, and together they make it the hardest tool here to try before you buy.
ahrefs.best_for: Solo operators who already know they want it.
ahrefs.watch_for: Team costs. Three users on Advanced is $449 plus two surcharged seats, not $449.

helpscout.headline: Full marks, and the trial does not ask for a card
helpscout.body: Free for five users on one inbox, then $25 a seat, or $21 annually. Fifteen days to try Standard or Plus with no card, no setup fee, and no minimum until the Pro tier. One of only a handful here that passes all eight tests.
helpscout.best_for: Small support teams who want to start free and scale without a sales call.
helpscout.watch_for: Pro carries a ten-seat minimum, so the jump from Plus is larger than the per-seat price suggests.

kit.headline: The most generous free tier in this entire set
kit.body: Free up to ten thousand subscribers. Not ten thousand emails, ten thousand subscribers. Creator is $33 a month at a thousand subscribers, or $390 annually, with a fourteen-day trial that needs no card. Full marks.
kit.best_for: Newsletter operators who want to prove the model before paying anything.
kit.watch_for: Price scales with list size, so the $33 headline is an entry point, not your steady-state bill.

wave.headline: Free accounting that is actually free
wave.body: Starter is $0 with no trial clock and no feature countdown. Pro is $19 a month or $190 annually. The money is made on payment processing at 2.9% plus 60 cents, which is disclosed plainly rather than buried.
wave.best_for: Sole traders and small businesses who invoice occasionally and do not want a subscription.
wave.watch_for: Processing fees are where the cost lives. If you take a lot of card payments, model that, not the subscription.

slack.headline: Clean per-seat pricing, one quote-only tier
slack.body: Free tier with a ninety-day message limit, Pro at $8.75 a seat or $7.25 annually, Business+ at $18 or $15. No seat minimums, no setup fee. The single point it drops is Enterprise+, which is quote-only.
slack.best_for: Teams who will live in Pro or Business+ and never need a quote.
slack.watch_for: The free tier's ninety-day history limit arrives quietly, and older messages become unreachable rather than deleted.

github.headline: Cheap, published, and honest about the free tier
github.body: Free is genuinely usable, Team is $4 a seat and Enterprise $21. Annual costs exactly twelve monthlies, so there is no penalty for staying flexible. The page notes pricing is for the first twelve months without publishing the rate after that.
github.best_for: Teams of any size; the free tier covers a surprising amount.
github.watch_for: That first-twelve-months footnote. Ask what year two costs before you commit a large seat count.

basecamp.headline: Flat rate, so headcount does not change the bill
basecamp.body: Freelancer $25, Studio $59, Pro $99 a month, and everyone is included. No per-user fees at all, which makes it the only tool here where adding people costs nothing. Trials run thirty days, forty-five on Unlimited, with no card.
basecamp.best_for: Growing teams tired of every new hire increasing four different bills.
basecamp.watch_for: Unlimited at $299 is billed annually only. Extra storage beyond the plan is $100 a month for 5TB.

bitwarden.headline: Cheapest credible password manager, with a real free tier
bitwarden.body: Free covers unlimited passwords. Teams is $4 a seat, Enterprise $6, and annual is exactly twelve monthlies on every tier, so there is no commitment premium anywhere. Personal Premium is $1.65 a month.
bitwarden.best_for: Teams who want managed password security without a per-seat argument.
bitwarden.watch_for: Trial length is not published on any business tier, so plan the evaluation window yourself.

buffer.headline: Priced per channel, which is unusual and mostly fair
buffer.body: Free covers three channels. Essentials is $5 and Team $10, both per channel rather than per user, with a 20% annual discount and a fourteen-day trial. Channels beyond ten cost less each.
buffer.best_for: Solo operators and small teams running a handful of accounts.
buffer.watch_for: Per-channel pricing scales fast. Ten channels on Team is $100 a month, not $10.

netlify.headline: Published seat prices, then credits on top
netlify.body: Free, Personal at $9 and Pro at $20 a member, all published. The catch is that every tier runs on a credit system for builds, bandwidth and compute, so the seat price is the floor rather than the bill. Enterprise is quote-only.
netlify.best_for: Developers who can predict their build and bandwidth usage.
netlify.watch_for: Auto-recharge credit packs. Understand the burn rate before enabling them.

framer.headline: Straight site pricing, expensive collaborators
framer.body: Basic $10 and Pro $30 a month for a site, published clearly. There is no annual discount at all, which is unusual and means monthly buyers are not punished. Extra editor seats are $20 a month each, more than the Basic site plan itself.
framer.best_for: Solo designers and small studios where one person edits.
framer.watch_for: Editor seats. A three-person team on Basic is $50 a month, not $10.

quickbooks.headline: Published prices, aggressive intro discount
quickbooks.body: Simple Start $38 through Advanced $340, all published, with a thirty-day trial. The wrinkle is the promotion: 50% off for three months means month four roughly doubles. User counts are capped per tier, from one on Simple Start to twenty-five on Advanced.
quickbooks.best_for: Businesses that will stay long enough for the intro rate to stop mattering.
quickbooks.watch_for: Budget from the list price, not the promotional one, and check the user cap against your headcount.

miro.headline: Clear pricing until the Enterprise wall
miro.body: Free covers three editable boards. Starter is $10 a member or $8 annually, Business $25 or $20, with a fourteen-day Business trial. Enterprise is quote-only and starts from thirty members.
miro.best_for: Teams under thirty who will stay on Business.
miro.watch_for: The thirty-member Enterprise floor. There is no middle tier between Business and a sales call.

figma.headline: Monthly exists on Professional and nowhere else
figma.body: Professional is $16 a full seat monthly. Organization at $55 and Enterprise at $90 are billed annually only, so the monthly-looking number is a twelve-month commitment. Seats are split three ways, full, dev and collaborator, which genuinely lowers cost for mixed teams.
figma.best_for: Design teams who can stay on Professional, or who have many view-only collaborators.
figma.watch_for: The annual-only wall above Professional, and Professional's own annual rate is not published at all.

calendly.headline: Honest at the bottom, a hard wall at the top
calendly.body: Free tier, Standard $10 a seat or $8.30 annually, Teams $16 or $12.80. All clean. Enterprise is quote-only, starts at $15,000 a year, and requires fifty seats, which is a very large step from a $16 plan.
calendly.best_for: Individuals and small teams; the paid tiers are genuinely priced for them.
calendly.watch_for: There is nothing between Teams and a $15,000 minimum commitment.

typeform.headline: The seat minimums climb faster than the price
typeform.body: Free covers a hundred responses. Basic is $39 or $28 annually with a fourteen-day trial. Then it stacks: Plus requires three seats, Business and Growth Flow require five. Business reads as $129 but cannot be bought for less than five seats.
typeform.best_for: Solo users on Basic, or teams already at five people.
typeform.watch_for: Response caps as much as seats. Basic includes only a hundred responses a month.

loom.headline: Simple pricing, generous free tier
loom.body: Starter is free for up to fifty members. Business is $18 a creator or $15 annually, Business plus AI is $24 or $20, both with a fourteen-day trial. Enterprise is quote-only.
loom.best_for: Teams where a few people record and many people watch; viewers are not charged.
loom.watch_for: The AI tier is a third more expensive. Check whether you need it before defaulting to it.

zapier.headline: Task-based pricing that is clear until the Team tier
zapier.body: Free covers a hundred tasks. Professional runs $29.99 to $73.50 monthly depending on task volume, or a third less annually, with a fourteen-day trial and no card. Team is $103.50 but carries a twenty-five seat minimum.
zapier.best_for: Individuals and small teams on Professional, where the pricing is genuinely transparent.
zapier.watch_for: Tasks, not Zaps, are the unit. A single busy automation can consume a tier.

vercel.headline: Twenty dollars, plus whatever you use
vercel.body: Hobby is free and Pro is $20 a seat with $20 of usage credit included. Everything past that is metered: edge requests, bandwidth, function invocations, build minutes, image transformations. Extra seats are another $20 each. Enterprise is quote-only.
vercel.best_for: Teams who have modelled their traffic and know the usage line.
vercel.watch_for: The seat price is the smallest part of a busy project's bill. Model the metered items first.

grammarly.headline: Cheap and clear, but only half the prices are published
grammarly.body: The free tier is real. Pro is $12 a member monthly with a seven-day trial that needs no card. What is missing is the annual rate, which is not published anywhere, and Enterprise, which is quote-only.
grammarly.best_for: Individuals and small teams on Pro.
grammarly.watch_for: You cannot compare the annual commitment, because Grammarly does not publish it.

freshbooks.headline: The team-member surcharge is the real cost
freshbooks.body: Lite $23, Plus $43, Premium $70, with a thirty-day trial. Straightforward until you add people: every extra team member is $11 a month on every tier. A four-person team on Plus is $76, not $43. Select is quote-only.
freshbooks.watch_for: The $11 per head. It is disclosed, but it sits well below the headline price.

airtable.headline: The monthly option is simply not offered
airtable.body: The free tier is generous. Team is $20 a seat and Business $45, but both are published as annual rates with no monthly figure at all, so the entry commitment is a year. Enterprise Scale is quote-only.
airtable.best_for: Teams committing for a year who will stay inside Team or Business.
airtable.watch_for: There is no way to buy a single month at a paid tier to trial it properly.

trello.headline: Cheap and honest, until Enterprise
trello.body: Free supports up to ten collaborators. Standard is $6 a user or $5 annually, Premium $12.50 or $10. All clean and all buyable one seat at a time. Enterprise is annual-only at $17.50 a user.
trello.best_for: Small teams; the free and Standard tiers cover most of what people actually use.
trello.watch_for: The free tier's ten-collaborator ceiling, which arrives sooner than the feature limits do.

xero.headline: The intro price is a tenth of the real one
xero.body: Early $25, Growing $55, Established $90, all published. The problem is the promotion: 90% off for six months means you pay $2.50 and then $25, a tenfold step-up at month seven. There is no free tier and no free trial listed.
xero.best_for: Businesses that have already decided and will absorb the month-seven increase.
xero.watch_for: Month seven. Budget from the list price and treat the discount as a rebate, not a rate.

zendesk.headline: Every price is a twelve-month commitment
zendesk.body: Support Team $19, Suite Team $55, Suite Professional $115 per agent, all shown as monthly figures and all billed annually. No monthly option is published on any tier, so Suite Professional is $1,380 per agent up front. Enterprise is quote-only.
zendesk.best_for: Support teams with budget approved for a full year.
zendesk.watch_for: The fourteen-day trial runs on Suite Professional, the most expensive published tier, which flatters the evaluation.

ghost.headline: Annual-only above the entry plan
ghost.body: Starter is $18 a month at a thousand members. Publisher at $29 and Business at $199 are published as annual rates only, with no monthly option shown. There is no free tier and no trial length published.
ghost.best_for: Publishers who know they are committing for a year.
ghost.watch_for: Member counts, not features, drive the tier. Growth moves you up the price list automatically.

surfer.headline: No free tier, no trial, and the seats stack
surfer.body: Discovery $49, Standard $99, Pro $182, Peace of Mind $299. All published, but there is no free tier and no free trial, so there is no way to evaluate it without paying. The minimums climb with the tier: one seat, then three, then five, then ten.
surfer.best_for: Agencies who already know the tool and have the headcount for the tier.
surfer.watch_for: Standard is not $99 for a solo user. It is $99 with a three-seat floor.
